history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: No published travel, tourism, or temple source documents a specific 'Shiva Temple'/'Shiv Mandir' in Mokokchung town; the identity, exact location, age, and history of this shrine could not be verified from web or map-listing sources, so this entry is provisional (verify). The town-level Hindu temple listing for Mokokchung (onefivenine.com) records only four temples - Sarvajanik Gorkha Mandir (Arkong), Laxminarayn Templ, Durga Mandir (NH-61) and Bishnu Mandir - none of which is a named Shiva temple; whether the CSV row refers to a shrine inside one of these (e.g. a Shiva shrine within the Gorkha mandir) or to a separate local mandir could not be established. The 'Shiv Mandir' documented at Kohima-Mokokchung Road, Wokha (indiainfo.net; inheritage.foundation) is in Wokha district, not Mokokchung, and must not be conflated with this entry. No CSV town/district/state correction is needed (Mokokchung, Mokokchung district, Nagaland); coordinates are the Mokokchung town centroid (verify). Mokokchung is the cultural heart of the Ao Naga people and is overwhelmingly Christian; Hindu shrines here are small community-serving temples of the non-tribal (largely Gorkha) population.

town_description: Mokokchung is the cultural heart of the Ao Naga people in the northern hills of Nagaland and the headquarters of Mokokchung district, sitting at about 1,325 m elevation on NH-2. Largely Christian (the Ao Nagas were evangelised from 1872), it has a small non-tribal Hindu population (largely Gorkha) served by a handful of small temples in and around town. Nearby attractions include the villages of Ungma, Longkhum and Chuchuyimlang, the Langpangkong caves and the Moatsu festival (May).
